claims.text: The relevant material family is fcc high-entropy alloys derived from the Fe-Co-Ni system, including CoCrFeMnNi.
Saturation magnetic moment is a primary property targeted for improvement.
Magnetic ordering temperature is also targeted for improvement.
High strength-ductility is intended to be maintained while magnetic properties are improved.
Longitudinal spin fluctuations strongly suppress the magnetic moments of Co, Fe, and Ni in the finite-temperature paramagnetic state.
Chemical disorder quenches the orbital magnetic moment contribution.
Competition between fcc and hcp phase stability makes the orbital moment contribution difficult to isolate.
Longitudinal spin fluctuations induce sizable magnetic moments for Co, Cr, and Ni in CoCrFeMnNi.
Longitudinal spin fluctuations cause a temperature-dependent reduction in saturation magnetization.
Longitudinal spin fluctuations affect phase stability and stacking-fault energy in fcc and hcp CoCrFeMnNi.
The Cantor alloy is usually a chemically disordered fcc solid solution over a wide temperature range below its solidus at ambient pressure.
CoCrFeMnNi has an enhanced strength-ductility combination as temperature decreases and retains outstanding cryogenic fracture toughness.
At cryogenic temperatures, hcp CoCrFeMnNi is energetically preferred over fcc CoCrFeMnNi, producing negative stacking-fault energy.
Controlled variation of Co, Ni, Fe, Mn, or Cr content and thermal processing can stabilize fcc while minimizing longitudinal spin fluctuations.
Longitudinal spin fluctuations in the fcc structure reduce the effective magnetic moment.
Cryogenic formation of hcp material alters the electronic structure and quenches orbital moments.
Stabilizing fcc and suppressing hcp formation will enhance both spin and orbital moment contributions.
A stabilized fcc Fe-Co-Ni-based HEA will exhibit a saturation magnetization greater than 1.5 μB per atom.
A stabilized fcc Fe-Co-Ni-based HEA will have a higher Curie temperature than the standard Cantor alloy.
Reduced longitudinal spin fluctuations and suppressed hcp formation will produce an orbital moment contribution greater than 0.1 μB per atom.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says longitudinal spin fluctuations strongly suppress or reduce magnetic moments, but it also says that they induce sizable moments for Co, Cr, and Ni. The cited evidence supports induction of sizable moments, not the asserted suppression.
